points.description: States that the block (body) of a do ... while statement always executes at least once.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if it says do...while runs the body before checking the condition but does not say 'at least once'.

points.description: Correctly contrasts with while: in a while loop the condition is tested before the body, so the block may execute zero times (not at all) if the condition is initially false.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if it only says while checks the condition first without stating the body may run zero times.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise fact that a do ... while body runs at least once, plus the contrast that a while body may run zero times because the condition is tested first. Vague wording such as 'they are different loops' or 'do while is more flexible' earns nothing. A wrong statement, for example saying while always runs once, loses the point it affects.
